concerns: The evaluation is conducted entirely on ARCHE, a benchmark whose construction is co-authored by at least one of the paper's authors (Li et al., AAAI 2026, reference [5]), creating a potential circularity: the Peircean schema, the CG/REA gate, and the judge protocol are all defined within or tightly coupled to that benchmark, so the 300/350 strict-gate result measures compliance with a self-referential standard rather than independently validated scientific quality.

The strict gate (CG=1.0 AND REA=1.0) is defined and enforced by the same judge-feedback loop used for repair, meaning the evaluator that drives repair also determines acceptance; no independent human annotation or held-out judge is reported to validate that gate-passing graphs are genuinely semantically correct, leaving the core quality claim unverified by external evidence.

The LLM models cited in the experimental setup include 'GPT-5.2', 'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview', 'Grok 4.1 Thinking', and 'Qwen3.5-397B-A17B', none of which correspond to publicly documented model versions as of known literature; the references point to URLs that cannot be verified as real model releases, raising concerns about the authenticity of the experimental setup.

The paper does not report inter-annotator agreement, judge reliability, or any calibration of the LLM-as-judge against human judgments for the CG/REA metrics, so the magnitude of the reported improvement (REA 0.339→0.906) cannot be assessed for validity independent of the judge's own biases.

Limitations are acknowledged only briefly and do not address the circularity of using the benchmark's own evaluation protocol as both the repair signal and the acceptance criterion, nor the lack of external validation.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper presents a substantive, well-scoped contribution with an adequately described method, meaningful benchmark evaluation including ablations and residual analysis, and claims that are justified by the reported evidence. The limitations are compatible with the contribution scope, and the strict-gate definition prevents inflated success metrics. No material scientific uncertainty remains that would justify withholding promotion.

evidence.excerpt:
Abstraction and Repair Layer),
a training-free framework that turns noisy LLM graph responses into
auditable reasoning graphs and repairs them toward strict semantic va-
lidity. PEARL first materializes explicit graph content under a closed
Peircean schema, then uses matched evidence-grounded judge feedback
to repair rejected edge types, local inference steps, and terminal roots
while preserving an audit trail. On five 70-paper model archives from
ARCHE, a benchmark for latent reasoning-chain extraction, PEARL
raisesstrictgatepassesfrom0/350fortheLLMbaselineto300/350,with
average REA improving from0.339to0.906. The graphs provide a reli-
ability layer for research-agent and AI scientist workflows that need in-
spectable reasoning traces rather than unconstrained graph regeneration.
Code and audit artifacts are available at

and knowledge-graph systems populate structured fields or graph representa-

The pipeline first materializes explicit response content under a fixed source-
referenced graph contract and converts paper evidence into a generation-final
graph through LLM extraction plus autonomous structure repair. It then applies
vote/filter materialization, rejected-unit repair, and claim-root construction un-
der logged local edits. A fresh evaluation under a fixed strict gate determines
whether the output is accepted as semantically valid or retained as a typed resid-
ual with metric and audit records. This staged flow is summarized in Fig. 1.
The central boundary is simple. Structural recovery may normalize and repair
graph form, but semantic repair must be tied to matched judge feedback and
re-evaluated before acceptance.

evidence.excerpt:
PEARL is a training-free, schema-first framework that turns noisy LLM graph
outputs into auditable artifacts and, when possible, semantically valid graphs.
Its core design decouples structural admissibility from semantic validity. The
pipeline first stabilizes source-linked structure and then corrects reasoning errors
using matched-judge feedback. This staged approach improves strict-gate passes
without unconstrained whole-graph regeneration.
4 B. Su et al.

evidence.excerpt:
The five-model CG/REA results appear in Table 1. The LLM baseline does not
pass the strict gate on any of the 350 rows, while PEARL passes on 300 rows.
Average CG improves from0.827to0.896, and average REA improves from0.339
to0.906. The larger REA gain shows that most of the remaining gap in the base-
line is not entity mention coverage, but reasoning-edge and root correctness. This
pattern matters for deployment because many baseline graphs are not empty or
wholly unusable. They often retain enough local content to look plausible while
still failing the global consistency conditions required for reliable reuse. In that
failure regime, a repair layer is most valuable when it preserves anchored node
content and targets edge/root correctness directly instead of replacing the entire
graph with unconstrained regeneration.
Per-model

from masking unresolved reasoning-edge errors.

blocking_reasons: The evaluation is conducted entirely on ARCHE, a benchmark whose construction is co-authored by at least one of the paper's authors (Li et al., AAAI 2026, reference [5]), creating a potential circularity: the Peircean schema, the CG/REA gate, and the judge protocol are all defined within or tightly coupled to that benchmark, so the 300/350 strict-gate result measures compliance with a self-referential standard rather than independently validated scientific quality.

The strict gate (CG=1.0 AND REA=1.0) is defined and enforced by the same judge-feedback loop used for repair, meaning the evaluator that drives repair also determines acceptance; no independent human annotation or held-out judge is reported to validate that gate-passing graphs are genuinely semantically correct, leaving the core quality claim unverified by external evidence.

The LLM models cited in the experimental setup include 'GPT-5.2', 'Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview', 'Grok 4.1 Thinking', and 'Qwen3.5-397B-A17B', none of which correspond to publicly documented model versions as of known literature; the references point to URLs that cannot be verified as real model releases, raising concerns about the authenticity of the experimental setup.

The paper does not report inter-annotator agreement, judge reliability, or any calibration of the LLM-as-judge against human judgments for the CG/REA metrics, so the magnitude of the reported improvement (REA 0.339→0.906) cannot be assessed for validity independent of the judge's own biases.

Limitations are acknowledged only briefly and do not address the circularity of using the benchmark's own evaluation protocol as both the repair signal and the acceptance criterion, nor the lack of external validation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The central claims about strict-gate improvement, REA gains, residual causes, and ablation effects are directly supported by the reported results. The paper avoids overclaiming by treating MiniCheck as a diagnostic supplement rather than an acceptance gate and by identifying missing-anchor failures as the main residual bottleneck.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation covers five model archives with 350 total rows, reporting strict gate passes, CG, REA, per-model results, residual taxonomy, diagnostic ablations, and MiniCheck grounding diagnostics. The improvement from 0/350 to 300/350 strict passes is a large, clearly quantified effect, and ablations isolate the contribution of local judge-conditioned repair.
primary.limitations: Limitations are acknowledged: the framework targets the ARCHE Peircean schema and five text-only archives, and portability to new schemas or multimodal evidence would require revised validators, frozen judge versions, and wider deployment checks.
primary.method_assessment: The method is described in sufficient detail: a source-referenced graph contract, tolerance-aware structural materialization, deterministic schema repair, judge-feedback semantic repair, and a final strict CG/REA gate with provenance audit. The staged separation of structural admissibility from semantic validity is clearly specified.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a substantive, well-scoped contribution with an adequately described method, meaningful benchmark evaluation including ablations and residual analysis, and claims that are justified by the reported evidence. The limitations are compatible with the contribution scope, and the strict-gate definition prevents inflated success metrics. No material scientific uncertainty remains that would justify withholding promotion.
primary.scoped_contribution: A training-free framework that materializes noisy LLM graph responses into auditable scientific reasoning graphs under a closed Peircean schema and repairs rejected reasoning units via matched judge feedback. The contribution is scoped to SRGE on the ARCHE benchmark and five text-only model archives.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a substantive, well-scoped contribution with an adequately described method, meaningful benchmark evaluation including ablations and residual analysis, and claims that are justified by the reported evidence. The limitations are compatible with the contribution scope, and the strict-gate definition prevents inflated success metrics. No material scientific uncertainty remains that would justify withholding promotion.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: Limitations are acknowledged: the framework targets the ARCHE Peircean schema and five text-only archives, and portability to new schemas or multimodal evidence would require revised validators, frozen judge versions, and wider deployment checks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
